Implements group_aggregate(records, key, aggregations) in core.py, applying
named sum/mean/count/min/max aggregations per group and returning one row per
group. Adds two supporting pure helpers in helpers.py: coerce_numeric and
merge_group_keys. Exports the new public API from __init__.py. Includes a
thorough test suite covering normal paths and edge cases (empty input,
malformed records, boundary values, error behavior).

args.title: Add group_aggregate with coerce_numeric and merge_group_keys helpers
args.body:
## Summary

Adds a `group_aggregate(records, key, aggregations)` function to the core module,
plus two supporting helpers in a new `helpers` module.

### Core feature
- `group_aggregate(records, key, aggregations)` — groups records by `key` and
  applies a dict of named aggregations mapping output field name to an
  `(operation, field)` pair. Supports `sum`, `mean`, `count`, `min`, `max`.
  Returns one record per group, in first-seen order. Raises `ValueError` for
  unknown operations and `KeyError` for missing group/aggregation fields.

### Helpers (`src/dataproc/helpers.py`)
- `coerce_numeric(value)` — safely converts values to a number, returning `None`
  for non-numeric input. Booleans are treated as non-numeric; numeric strings
  are parsed.
- `merge_group_keys(records, keys)` — builds a composite (tuple) grouping key
  per record from multiple fields.

### Other
- Exported the new public API from `src/dataproc/__init__.py`.
- Added test suites: `tests/test_group_aggregate.py` and `tests/test_helpers.py`
  covering normal paths, empty input, malformed records, boundary values, and
  purity (no input mutation).

All functions are pure and follow the existing style. 46 tests pass locally.
Did not touch any forbidden infrastructure files.
